parts.text: According to IDSA, name the indications for conducting COVID-19 serology (Antibody testing).

questions.model_answer: IDSA-recommended indications for COVID-19 serologic (antibody) testing: (1) evaluation of patients with a high clinical suspicion of COVID-19 when molecular (NAAT) testing is negative and it has been >2 weeks since symptom onset, (2) diagnosis of multisystem inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C/MIS-A) in patients with suspected recent SARS-CoV-2 infection, (3) seroprevalence/epidemiologic surveillance studies, (4) evaluation for potential convalescent plasma donation. Serology is not recommended to diagnose acute infection or to determine immune status/need for vaccination.

parts.text: List 3 indications as per the IDSA guidelines for use of SARS-CoV2 serology

cohort_answer.text: When laboratory confirmation is required for clinical or epidemiological purposes (testing COVID IgG or total antibody at least 3-4 weeks after symptom onset); Confirmation of infection in symptomatic patients with high clinical suspicion when molecular testing was repeatedly negative or unable to be performed; In work up of suspected pediatric MIS-C including both IgG and NAAT
